main_text.p: tet[?] usurpat, quàm Apostoli & Apostolici Viri, eorúmque etiam discipuli. Hic enim duo illa nomina plané eodem sensu accipit, quo à tertij sæculi, & sequentium Christianis ad hæc usque tempora accepta fuisse & scimus, & libenter concedimus: sic nimirum, ut duas dignitates à se invicem distinctas significent: Episcopus-que is intelligatur, qui Presbyter quidem ipse quoque est; sed & Presbyterio præest, & in eorum Collegio caput est; Presbyter verò is sit qui Episcopo subest. Unde necessario exsurgunt tres in Ecclesiâ ministrorum ordines; Episcopus, primus & summus: Presbyter, secundus & medius; Diaconus denique tertius & infimus: Argumentum duabus constat propositionibus, quarum prior usum ac consuetudinem spectat Epistolici Ignatij in Episcopi & Presbyteri nominibus usurpandis; posterior usum ac consuetudinem Apostolorum, & Apostolicorum Virorum, eorúmque etiam discipulorum planè diversam; Utrámque propositionem fusè pro-bat Dallæus, illam pag. 386. 387. 388. Hanc verò in sequentibus. Videamus jam quibus exceptionibus hoc Dallæi argumētum refellere nituntur Viri Eruditi: Inchoabo à Societatis Sorbonicæ Theologo, qui in Epistolam ad Magnesianos[?]

page.notes: The first word "tet" is badly printed; it is probably "ter" with a damaged r, so it is marked [?]. The printed "p ro-bat" appears to be "pro-bat" with a stray "p" before the hyphen, which is kept as the printer's word split. The final word "Magnesianos" has a flourish at the line end, which may be a special abbreviation sign, so it is marked [?]. Italic runs follow the printed type. The "Digitized by Google" watermark at the bottom right is left out.
